record.question:
A homogeneous, unweighted EC2 Auto Scaling group serves a stateless application behind an ALB. The company requires each eligible scale-in action to remove exactly one instance when the group's average CPU utilization is 15% or lower for three consecutive one-minute periods. A cooldown must allow capacity to settle between actions, and the group must never scale below its configured minimum.

Which solution implements this rule with the least custom code?

options.text: Create scheduled scaling actions that decrease desired capacity by one at fixed times when low usage is usually expected.

Enable detailed monitoring for existing and future group instances. Create a CloudWatch CPU alarm with the specified threshold and evaluation periods. Attach a simple scaling policy with ChangeInCapacity set to -1, configure its cooldown, and retain the group minimum.
Run a custom Lambda scheduler that reads CPU metrics, maintains evaluation and cooldown state, and calls the Auto Scaling API to decrement desired capacity.
Configure a target tracking policy with a CPU target of 15% and rely on it to remove exactly one instance for every qualifying low-CPU condition.

explanation.text:
<<2>> is correct. Detailed monitoring supplies one-minute EC2 CPU measurements; basic monitoring supplies five-minute measurements. The alarm defines the metric condition and observation window, while the simple scaling policy defines the fixed decrement. In this unweighted group, `ChangeInCapacity = -1` removes one capacity unit, which is one instance. The cooldown and group minimum constrain subsequent actions.

<<1>> responds to time rather than the measured CPU condition.

<<3>> can implement the rule, but duplicates native alarm and scaling behavior with custom state and code.

<<4>> pursues a utilization target and calculates capacity adjustments dynamically; it does not promise the requested fixed one-instance decrement.

For simple and step scaling, you create and manage the CloudWatch alarms. Target tracking manages its own alarms and is often suitable for ordinary utilization targets, but that is a different policy objective. Allow ALB deregistration and graceful shutdown, and evaluate scale-out thresholds to prevent repeated scale-in and scale-out oscillation.

Official AWS references (checked September 18, 2026): [Fixed scaling adjustments](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-scaling-simple-step.html). [Scaling cooldowns](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-scaling-cooldowns.html). [EC2 monitoring granularity](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/enable-as-instance-metrics.html).

diagram_alt: A qualifying low-CPU alarm drives a fixed decrement, bounded by minimum capacity and cooldown.

sources.supports: User-managed CloudWatch alarms, ChangeInCapacity semantics, cooldown versus target tracking, and anti-flapping guidance
Simple scaling cooldown behavior and settling periods
One-minute EC2 CPU measurement requires detailed monitoring on existing instances and the launch template for future instances; alarm periods must match monitoring granularity.

editorial_notes: Preserved answer 2. Repaired the explanation that conflated simple scaling with target tracking, specified an unweighted group and evaluation periods, and made fixed decrement, cooldown and minimum constraints explicit.
Root review added detailed monitoring for existing and future instances so three consecutive one-minute CPU periods have the necessary metric resolution.
